source_refs.note: Exercise 14.1, Question 7: book page 267 (PDF 272); answer key PDF 311 (book page 306).

blocks.prompt: 7 If \(\underline{u} = x\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = \underline{i} + y\underline{j} - 3\underline{k}\) and \(\underline{w} = -2\underline{i} - 3\underline{j}\) represent the sides of a triangle, find the value of \(x\) and \(y\).
blocks.explanation:
Three vectors form a triangle, so one of them is the sum of the other two (triangle law of addition).
We must find the unknowns \(x\) and \(y\).
Plan: take \(\underline{w} = \underline{u} + \underline{v}\) (the only arrangement the known \(\underline{k}\) parts allow besides going round the triangle), compare components, solve, check.
steps:
Given: \(\underline{u} = x\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = \underline{i} + y\underline{j} - 3\underline{k}\), \(\underline{w} = -2\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 0\underline{k}\) are the sides of a triangle.
To find: \(x\) and \(y\).
Method: Triangle law: placing \(\underline{u}\) and \(\underline{v}\) head to tail, the third side is \(\underline{w} = \underline{u} + \underline{v}\). Equal vectors have equal components.

Add \(\underline{u}\) and \(\underline{v}\)
\[\underline{u} + \underline{v} = (x + 1)\underline{i} + (2 + y)\underline{j}\]
\[\quad + (3 - 3)\underline{k}\]
Why: Matching components are added; the unknowns stay inside their brackets.

Set equal to \(\underline{w}\) and compare
\[\underline{i}: x + 1 = -2\]
\[\underline{j}: 2 + y = -3\]
\[\underline{k}: 3 - 3 = 0\]
Why: Two vectors are equal only when their \(\underline{i}\), \(\underline{j}\) and \(\underline{k}\) parts are equal. The \(\underline{k}\) equation is already true, so this arrangement is consistent.

Solve
\[x = -2 - 1 = -3\]
\[y = -3 - 2 = -5\]
Why: Each equation has one unknown, so we just move the number across.

Check
\[\underline{u} = -3\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\]
\[\underline{v} = \underline{i} - 5\underline{j} - 3\underline{k}\]
\[\underline{u} + \underline{v} = -2\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} = \underline{w} \;\checkmark\]
Why: With these values the sum of the first two sides is exactly the third side.

Another arrangement
\[\underline{u} + \underline{v} + \underline{w} = \underline{0}\]
\[\Rightarrow x - 1 = 0,\ y - 1 = 0\]
\[\Rightarrow x = 1,\ y = 1\]
Why: The question does not say how the sides are arranged. If all three are taken head to tail round the triangle, they add to the zero vector and give \(x = 1,\ y = 1\). The answer key uses \(\underline{w} = \underline{u} + \underline{v}\); in an exam, state the relation you use.
blocks.final_answer: \(x = -3,\ y = -5\) (taking \(\underline{w} = \underline{u} + \underline{v}\), as the answer key does; with \(\underline{u} + \underline{v} + \underline{w} = \underline{0}\) one gets \(x = 1,\ y = 1\))
